title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1966 letter to Tate on crystals, ch. 2. G(A) is the universal vector extension of an abelian scheme A/S. Its Lie algebra is (H^1_DR(A/S))^vee, with the Gauss–Manin connection. 'Stratification' means Grothendieck's descent datum on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal, without divided powers. Equivalently it is a crystal on the infinitesimal site. In char 0 this is just an integrable connection; in char p it is much stronger (in modern terms an F-divided or 'stratified' bundle).

The page closes a bracket from the previous page: stratified modules play the role of l-adic sheaves and share their rigidity. It then returns to the question of whether, for an 'ordinary' abelian scheme in char p, G(A) does not vary infinitesimally.

Claim: one might still have a canonical functorial stratification of H^1_DR on the ordinary locus. But it cannot come from a crystal on S in the strong sense. That sense means it persists over every infinitesimal thickening of S, including thickenings not of char p, with connection equal to Gauss–Manin.

Proof sketch:
1. Take the modular scheme S (with level structure) localized at Z_p. It is smooth over Z_p, hence a regular 2-dimensional scheme.
2. Remove the finitely many supersingular closed points (Hasse invariant zero) to get S'.
3. The hypothetical crystal gives a stratification of H^1_DR over the p-adic completion of S'.
4. This glues with the char-0 Gauss–Manin stratification on the generic fibre S_Q.
5. By purity (the removed points have codimension 2) and a formal gluing argument, it extends over all of S.
6. Restricting to the special fibre gives a stratification of H^1_DR over the entire modular curve in char p, supersingular points included. Section 2.7 had shown this is absurd.

Conclusion: isocrystals, and possibly stratified modules in char p, may be the right tools for families of abelian varieties. The (infinitesimal, non-PD) crystal notion is 'irrémédiablement trop fine', even for ordinary families. It may work only over a point, i.e. the spectrum of a possibly imperfect field, best for ordinary abelian varieties.

To use crystals over general bases one would have to restrict the families severely, by prescribing the infinitesimal variation of G(A). He likens this to Serre's study of deformations of abelian varieties, possibly with given complex multiplication, with prescribed tangent space and CM action.

The next page (ch. 3) transposes G(A) to p-divisible groups: the universal extension by the vector group of t_{Phi*}, with Lie algebra an extension of t_Phi by t^vee_{Phi*}.

Historically, this page records the failure of the divided-power-free notion of crystal. That failure is exactly what forced the passage to the crystalline site with divided powers (Grothendieck's IHES 1966 talk 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Berthelot's thesis). With divided powers, the 'non-variation of G(A)' becomes true: Grothendieck, ICM/Montréal 1970; Mazur–Messing 1974.
errors: The argument concerns crystals/stratifications without divided powers. With divided powers the hoped-for statement is true in full generality, ordinary or not: H^1_DR and the universal extension E(A) are crystals on the nilpotent PD crystalline site (Mazur–Messing 1974; Grothendieck–Messing). So the verdict 'la notion de cristal semble irrémédiablement trop fine' is only correct for the non-PD notion; it is superseded.

A much shorter argument is available, and it is stronger. A stratification whose underlying connection is Gauss–Manin forces the p-curvature to vanish. By Katz's formula (1970), the p-curvature of Gauss–Manin is the Frobenius-twisted Kodaira–Spencer map, which is nonzero on the modular curve, including on the ordinary locus. So even on the ordinary locus no stratification compatible with Gauss–Manin exists. The purity/gluing detour through Z_p and Q is unnecessary.

The step 'se recollerait ... ce qui doit impliquer le prolongement sur S de façon assez formelle' is only sketched. Gluing over the p-adic completion and the generic fibre needs a Beauville–Laszlo/fpqc-type argument plus Hartogs extension at codimension-2 points; it is plausible but not given.

He writes 'sauf erreur' and the previous page admits a gap: whether the char-p stratification would be compatible with Frobenius. So the contradiction with 2.7 is, by his own admission, not fully nailed down.

ideas.what: Stratification (descent data on all infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal) as an analogue of l-adic sheaves sharing their rigidity; in char p it is far stronger than a connection
ideas.modern_name: Crystals on the infinitesimal site / stratified (F-divided) bundles; rigidity of D-modules with full stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1966/68); Gieseker 1975 (flat bundles in char p); dos Santos; Esnault–Mehta
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), notes by Coates–Jussila

ideas.what: Non-existence of a stratification/infinitesimal crystal structure on H^1_DR of the modular family in char p compatible with Gauss–Manin; hence non-PD crystals are too fine
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the infinitesimal site in char p; nonvanishing p-curvature of Gauss–Manin (Katz) as the obstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motivating divided powers), Berthelot; Katz 1970 for the p-curvature formula
ideas.where_published: The general point is in Grothendieck 1968 (Dix exposés); this specific modular-curve argument is presumably only in the Tate letter

ideas.what: Gluing char-0 stratification with one on the p-adic completion of the ordinary locus, then extending over supersingular points by codimension-2 purity
ideas.modern_name: Beauville–Laszlo/formal gluing plus Hartogs extension for vector bundles on regular 2-dimensional schemes

ideas.what: Crystals best suited to a base that is a point (spectrum of an imperfect field), especially for ordinary abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Breen–Messing; de Jong (Dieudonné modules over non-perfect bases)

ideas.what: Universal vector extension G(A) whose Lie algebra is dual to H^1_DR, and the question of its infinitesimal invariance (crystalline nature)
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline nature of the universal extension; Dieudonné crystal; Grothendieck–Messing deformation theory
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970/74); ICM Nice 1970

ideas.what: Restricting families by prescribing the tangent space and the CM action on it (Serre's viewpoint)
ideas.modern_name: Determinant/signature (Kottwitz) condition for PEL moduli; Hodge filtration as deformation parameter

missed.claim: A documented intermediate stage in the invention of crystalline cohomology. Grothendieck explicitly concludes that crystals without divided powers are hopeless for families of abelian varieties, even ordinary ones. The argument is a concrete one via the modular curve over Z_p, purity, and supersingular points. This is a historiographical detail; the mathematics was superseded by the PD crystalline site.
missed.quote: celle de cristal elle-même semble irrémédiablement trop fine, même en se restreignant à des familles de VA "ordinaires" en car p>0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows that the obstruction which motivated divided powers was found by testing on the modular family. Mathematically it is subsumed by Katz's p-curvature formula.

missed.claim: He leaves open a canonical functorial stratification on H^1_DR over the ordinary locus that is not compatible with Gauss–Manin. This foreshadows the unit-root splitting over the ordinary locus. One can take the F-divided bundles attached to the étale part and the multiplicative part of A[p^∞], or Dwork–Katz unit-root F-crystals. Grothendieck does not make this link here, and it is not clear the specific question was ever formulated in these terms.
missed.quote: s'il n'est pas exclu que le H^1_DR admette une stratification canonique fonctorielle, il me semble cependant exclu ... que celle-ci provienne d'un cristal
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The ordinary-locus picture (Serre–Tate coordinates, Dwork's unit-root crystal, Katz 1973) is well developed, so little would be new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a pre-divided-power argument that is historically interesting but superseded. Grothendieck's own PD crystals, Mazur–Messing, and Katz's p-curvature results settle or subsume it. The modular-curve purity argument is a nice unpublished detail but carries no new mathematics today.
